# buttons.url

Build a native button that opens a URL.

## Signature

```python
def buttons.url(text: str, url: str) -> KeyboardButtonUrl
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Python type | Default | Passing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `str` | `Required` | Positional or keyword |
| `url` | `str` | `Required` | Positional or keyword |

### text

Literal text for this operation. No implicit Markdown or HTML parser is applied. Pass explicit native entities where the signature supports them; unsupported parse_mode/formatting keywords are not accepted.

### url

Nonempty URL string used by the native URL button. The builder does not fetch or validate the remote resource; Telegram applies URL/domain restrictions.

## Returns

types.KeyboardButtonUrl.

## Example

```python
from gramflux import Client, Session, buttons, filters
from gramflux.raw import types

button = buttons.url("Project", "https://github.com/gramflux/gramflux")
```

## Constraints and failure behavior

Both strings must be nonempty. This helper does not visit the URL or create callback events for the click.

These examples assume a previously constructed client where one is used. Builders and selectors do not make a network request by themselves. Invalid builder/selector inputs raise ConfigurationError or the underlying Python argument/regex error. Session I/O errors arise when storage is actually opened during connect.
